title: Spaced Repetition for Technical Concepts
content: Spaced repetition optimizes long-term retention by reviewing material at increasing intervals. For coding interviews: Day 1 - learn new concept, Day 3 - first review, Day 7 - second review, Day 14 - third review, Day 30 - final review. Apply to: algorithm patterns, system design concepts, behavioral stories. Use active recall: explain concepts without looking, implement algorithms from memory, draw system diagrams. Track difficulty: easy concepts get longer intervals, hard concepts get shorter intervals.
when_to_use: Long-term preparation (2+ months), retaining large amounts of information, preventing forgetting of previously learned concepts
implementation_tips: Use flashcards for quick concept reviews
Focus on weak areas more frequently

title: Pomodoro Technique for Coding Practice
content: Use focused 25-minute coding sessions with 5-minute breaks to maintain concentration and prevent burnout. Structure: 25 min problem-solving → 5 min break → 25 min implementation → 5 min break → 25 min optimization → 15 min break. During breaks: stretch, hydrate, avoid screens. After 4 pomodoros, take longer 15-30 minute break. Track progress: problems solved per session, concepts learned, areas of struggle. Adjust timing based on problem complexity.
when_to_use: Daily practice sessions, maintaining focus during long study periods, preventing mental fatigue

title: Progressive Mock Interview Strategy
content: Build interview confidence through structured mock interview progression. Week 1-2: Solo practice with timer, focus on problem-solving approach. Week 3-4: Record yourself explaining solutions, review communication clarity. Week 5-6: Practice with friends or online platforms, get feedback. Week 7-8: Professional mock interviews with experienced engineers. Focus areas: problem understanding, solution approach, code implementation, optimization discussion, time management.
when_to_use: Final 2 months of preparation, building interview confidence, practicing communication skills
implementation_tips: Start with easier problems for confidence

title: Algorithm Pattern Recognition Training
content: Master common algorithm patterns to quickly identify solution approaches. Core patterns: Two Pointers, Sliding Window, Fast & Slow Pointers, Merge Intervals, Cyclic Sort, Tree BFS/DFS, Binary Search, Top K Elements, K-way Merge, Dynamic Programming. Study method: learn pattern → solve 5-10 similar problems → identify pattern variations → practice mixed problems. Create pattern cheat sheet with templates and example problems.
when_to_use: Building problem-solving speed, recognizing solution patterns quickly, systematic algorithm learning
implementation_tips: Practice identifying patterns in new problems

title: System Design Building Blocks Approach
content: Master system design by learning fundamental building blocks, then combining them for complex systems. Core blocks: Load Balancers, Databases (SQL/NoSQL), Caches, Message Queues, CDNs, API Gateways, Microservices. Study approach: understand each component deeply → learn when to use each → practice combining components → design complete systems. Create reference architecture diagrams for common patterns.
when_to_use: Preparing for senior roles, system design interviews, understanding large-scale architecture
implementation_tips: Start with simple systems, add complexity

title: STAR Method for Behavioral Questions
content: Structure behavioral responses using STAR: Situation (context), Task (your responsibility), Action (what you did), Result (outcome and learning). Prepare 8-10 stories covering: leadership, conflict resolution, failure/learning, innovation, teamwork, challenging project. Each story should be 2-3 minutes, specific and quantifiable. Practice variations: same story for different question types, emphasizing different aspects based on the question focus.
when_to_use: Behavioral interview preparation, structuring experience stories, demonstrating soft skills
implementation_tips: Write out stories in STAR format

title: Weakness-Focused Improvement Strategy
content: Identify and systematically address weak areas for maximum improvement. Assessment: solve diverse problems, track success rate by topic, identify patterns in mistakes. Focus strategy: spend 60% time on weak areas, 30% on medium areas, 10% on strong areas. Weak area approach: study theory → solve easy problems → gradually increase difficulty → mixed practice. Track progress weekly and adjust focus areas.
when_to_use: Targeted skill improvement, efficient use of limited study time, addressing specific knowledge gaps
implementation_tips: Seek help for persistent weak areas
Balance weakness focus with confidence building

title: Strategic Company Research Framework
content: Research target companies systematically to tailor preparation and demonstrate genuine interest. Research areas: company mission/values, recent news/products, engineering culture, interview process, common questions, technology stack. Sources: company website, engineering blogs, Glassdoor, Blind, LinkedIn employees, GitHub repositories. Create company-specific preparation plan: align behavioral stories with company values, practice relevant technical problems, prepare thoughtful questions about the role and team.
when_to_use: Targeting specific companies, tailoring interview preparation, demonstrating company knowledge
